ratings_why.fun: Voting to the scouted opponent is a real choice each turn, but the flood build fades late because the water grows by about 1 a turn while Health grows much faster, and the Drain build is mostly plain stats and gold.
ratings_why.distinct: No tribe acts on both boards at once or cares about a unit's Health against a shared waterline, and Dive turning your own sinking into an upside is fresh.

verdict_why: Drowning reads two ways between the keyword and Tiddy Mun, and the Raise build needs a late-game reason to keep flooding.

points.text: The Drowning keyword says it keeps working all fight, but Tiddy Mun only drowns at Start of Combat. Say on the card whether he gives Drowning for the whole fight.

The water is a sum of Levels that climbs about 1-3 a turn, so by Tier 5-6 most enemy units stand far above it. Let some late payoff raise the water by a share of a unit's stats, so High Water still bites in the late game.

Board Almoner and Stretch-Holder pull against each other: the Holder lifts Health above your Level, which turns off the Almoner. That tension is good; a build line that says so would help players see it.
The Drain build pays in stats and gold and fights in dry land, so it plays like a generic buffer tribe. One Drain payoff that uses the empty gauge in the fight would keep it on theme.
Keeper of the Overflow is the best bridge in the tribe: draining for stats while still flooding the fight. Consider moving it to Tier 3 so the hybrid line starts earlier.

standouts.why: Master of the Nine Mills pays for every change either way, so the Seesaw build gets a capstone that grows the whole board, with a cap that keeps the golden near x4.
The Winter Raft turns the enemy sinking into board-wide fight stats, a Tier 5 combat engine that does its job.
Keeper of the Overflow links the two halves of the tribe in one card.

weakest.why: Gauge-Keeper of Stillwater only doubles a Level of maybe 6-10 by Tier 5, which is small next to late Health, and it sinks your own short units too.
Ditch Coot adds 1 water, which rarely matters past the early turns.
Schouw-Walker is a plain buffer with no tie to the water or the Vote.

flags.note: Hendrika doubles every Vote source; with Nine Mills, Sail-Setter and Kobus that is about 6 changes and +6/+6 to the board each turn. Hot but capped at nine.
Penningmeester Hiske with Sluiswacht and Hendrika can pay 4-6 gold a turn, and uncapped carried gold could chain triples.
Overflow never resets, so a long Drain game can flood every fight while the Level stays below 0.
Whether Tiddy Mun's drowning lasts all fight, as the keyword says, or happens once at Start of Combat.
